stories.headline: US bombs IRGC radar and air-defense sites; Iran hits US bases in Jordan, Iraq and Bahrain

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said it began striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets in Iran at 1600 GMT on Tuesday, September 1, citing IRGC attempted attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and on American service members.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. military said it began striking Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets in Iran at 1600 GMT on Tuesday. 'The strikes follow recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members deployed to the region,' CENTCOM said.

key_facts.fact: CENTCOM said Tuesday evening it had completed the barrage against Iranian military targets including air defense sites, radar systems and maritime assets; one US strike hit a home hosting a wedding, killing five people and wounding dozens, local officials said.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. Central Command said in a statement Tuesday evening that it had completed the latest barrage against Iranian military targets including air defense sites, radar systems and maritime assets. One U.S. strike hit a home hosting a wedding, killing five people and wounding dozens, local officials said.

key_facts.fact: Iran retaliated the same day: the IRGC said it launched a heavy ballistic missile attack on a US Marine Corps base in Jordan and 'killed a large number of U.S. forces' — the US said there were no casualties — and also struck US bases in Erbil, Iraq and a US base in Bahrain with drones, while Kuwait's army said its air defenses engaged a hostile drone.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it launched a heavy ballistic missile attack on the U.S. Marine Corps base in Jordan and 'killed a large number of U.S. forces.' ... Iranian media also reported the country's military targeted a U.S. base in Bahrain with a large-scale drone attack, and the Kuwaiti army reported its air defences were responding to a hostile drone attack.

key_facts.fact: Global oil prices rose more than $4 a barrel on Tuesday, settling at a five-week high, after the exchange of fire and Monday's attacks on two tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: The strikes followed a weekend exchange of fire — the first since July — and attacks on Monday on two tankers leaving the Strait of Hormuz, the global oil supply waterway that Iran has effectively closed to shipping. Global oil prices rose more than $4 a barrel on Tuesday, settling at a five-week high.

key_facts.fact: Trump told Fox News the US had struck Iranian radars Tehran was trying to rebuild and played down the prospect of another ceasefire, writing that he 'couldn't care less' if Iran signed an agreement and claiming 'almost total control of the Hormuz Strait.' He had warned that if Iran retaliated 'they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'I couldn't care less if they sign a worthless, to them, agreement. I like our position now much better, with almost total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing,' Trump wrote on social media.

key_facts.fact: Speaking at the SCO summit in Bishkek the same day, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Tehran would 'immediately reciprocate' if Washington returned to the June memorandum of understanding, under which Iran was to clear Hormuz of mines and the US to end its naval blockade and lift sanctions.
key_facts.excerpt: 'I am stating clearly that if the US returns to its commitments under the memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately reciprocate,' Pezeshkian said, according to IRNA.

key_facts.fact: The Institute for the Study of War assessed that the CENTCOM strikes focused on radars Iran uses to detect vessels transiting the strait, and that hitting them will likely impose operational constraints on Iranian efforts to disrupt shipping.
key_facts.excerpt: The CENTCOM strikes appeared to focus on assets that Iran uses to sense ships to strike. ... US strikes on radars will likely impose operational constraints on Iranian forces attempting to disrupt shipping in the strait.

stories.headline: SCO leaders sign Bishkek Declaration condemning the war on Iran as Xi calls multipolarity irreversible

key_facts.fact: On September 1 in Bishkek, leaders of the 10 SCO member states signed the Bishkek Declaration marking the bloc's 25th anniversary, approved a protocol amending the SCO Charter and adopted 28 outcome documents covering security, economic and cultural cooperation.
key_facts.excerpt: Leaders of the SCO member states signed and issued the Bishkek Declaration on the 25th Anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, approved the Protocol on Amending and Supplementing the Charter of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, the Regulations on the SCO Universal Center for Countering Security Challenges and Threats, and the Regulations on the SCO Anti-drug Center, and adopted 28 outcome documents.

key_facts.fact: The joint statement condemned the US and Israel's war on Iran and Western sanctions on member states. Signatories included Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, Narendra Modi, Masoud Pezeshkian and Shehbaz Sharif.
key_facts.excerpt: Leaders of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) have signed a joint statement condemning the US and Israel's war on Iran and Western sanctions on some of their members, after a two-day summit in Kyrgyzstan's capital, Bishkek.

key_facts.fact: Xi Jinping told the summit that multipolarity is an 'irreversible trend' and criticised 'hegemony, unilateralism and protectionism,' saying 'protectionism and decoupling have no future.'
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking at the summit, Xi said multipolarity was an 'irreversible trend' and described sovereign equality and mutual respect as fundamental principles of a multipolar world. ... 'Protectionism and decoupling have no future,' Xi said.

key_facts.fact: The document package included regulations for a new Universal Center for Countering Security Challenges and Threats, an action plan for ports and logistics centres through 2030, a Green Technology Corridor programme, a declaration on nuclear security and a joint statement on cooperation in energy systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Signatories adopted regulations for a new Universal Center for Countering Challenges and Threats to the Security of SCO Member States ... An action plan for developing ports and logistics centers of member territories through 2030 was also signed, alongside a 'Green Technology Corridor' cooperation program.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine was not mentioned in the declaration, and the summit stopped short of launching the proposed SCO Development Bank — no founding agreement, capital commitment or launch date was produced.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine was not mentioned in the declaration ... The Bishkek Declaration records progress toward creating an SCO Development Bank among interested member states during Kyrgyzstan's chairmanship, though the wording is qualified. The summit did not produce a founding agreement, capital commitment, or a launch date.

key_facts.fact: Modi used his address to call terrorism 'a grave challenge to all of humanity' and demanded an end to 'double standards' on the issue; Pakistan takes over the rotating chairmanship and will host the next heads-of-state council in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: On Tuesday, India's Modi described terrorism as a 'grave challenge to all of humanity', and asked countries to steer clear of 'double standards' on the issue.

key_facts.fact: In a bilateral on the sidelines, Modi told Putin: 'We must move from endless war to the end of war, to the cessation of hostilities,' while both sides confirmed work toward a $5 billion bilateral trade target by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Modi and Putin held a bilateral on the sidelines ahead of the plenary, discussing energy, fertilizer trade, defense cooperation, and bilateral trade targets. Indian and Russian officials confirmed both sides are working toward a USD 5 billion bilateral trade target by 2030.

stories.headline: Putin and Zelensky trade threats as Russia fires 174 drones and Kyiv vows to close Russian airspace

key_facts.fact: Starting at 18:00 on September 1, Russia launched 174 attack drones — about half of them jet-powered Shahed variants, plus S8000 Banderol, Gerbera and decoy drones — along with two Iskander-M ballistic missiles from Crimea and two Kh-59/69 air-launched missiles, mainly at the Kyiv and Odesa regions.
key_facts.excerpt: starting at 18:00 Tuesday, September 1, Russian forces launched ... two Iskander-M ballistic missiles from temporarily occupied Crimea; two Kh-59/69 guided air-launched missiles ... 174 attack drones, including Shahed-type UAVs (about half of them jet-powered).

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian air defenses shot down or jammed 141 of the 174 weapons; hits were recorded at 16 locations, with debris falling at four more.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's air defense neutralized 141 out of the 174 weapons used by Russian forces to attack Ukraine overnight on September 2. Hits by enemy missiles and combat drones were recorded at 16 locations.

key_facts.fact: Russian strikes on Dnipro killed two civilians and wounded six, hitting food warehouses belonging to a retail chain — part of a pattern of strikes on food depots that has left some supermarket shelves empty.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian aerial attacks overnight and during daylight Wednesday killed two civilians and wounded six in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials said, while the Kyiv and Odesa regions bore the brunt of Moscow's latest strikes.

key_facts.fact: In Odesa the barrage damaged a 24-storey residential building, destroying apartments on several floors and wounding eight people including a child, and caused a power outage that halted electric public transport.
key_facts.excerpt: Officials in the southern Ukraine region of Odesa reported that the attack damaged a 24-storey residential building, destroying apartments on several floors and wounding eight people, including a child. ... The barrage also caused a power outage that halted electric-powered public transport.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky warned foreign airlines that flying over Russia is unsafe because of Ukrainian long-range drone attacks, saying 'Russian airspace will effectively be closing' and that the pressure is meant to force Moscow into peace talks.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy warned foreign airlines that flying in Russia is not safe because of Ukrainian long-range drone attacks, saying that 'Russian airspace will'

key_facts.fact: At a late-night news conference on the sidelines of the SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan, Putin accused Zelensky of 'state terrorism' and said 'We don't negotiate with terrorists.'
key_facts.excerpt: Putin accused Zelenskyy of 'state terrorism' and said: 'We don't negotiate with terrorists.' At a late-night news conference on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan, Putin also addressed reports that the Ukrainian military had used British-made drones to strike targets inside Russia.

key_facts.fact: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defenses destroyed 130 Ukrainian drones overnight over 11 Russian regions, Crimea and the Black Sea; Ukrainian strikes killed two people and wounded 16 in Belgorod, where officials counted 140 hits in 24 hours.
key_facts.excerpt: Meanwhile in Russia, air defences destroyed 130 Ukrainian drones overnight, the Defence Ministry said on Wednesday. ... Ukrainian drone attacks killed two people in Russia's Belgorod border region and wounded 16 more, acting governor Aleksand Shuvaev said.

key_facts.fact: Germany on Tuesday blamed Russia for an attempted attack last month at Leipzig/Halle Airport using a drone laden with explosives, as European officials weigh a response to what they call Moscow's campaign of continental sabotage.
key_facts.excerpt: Germany on Tuesday blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month using a drone laden with explosives.

stories.headline: Uber cuts 3,300 jobs, 10% of staff, in its deepest layoff since 2020 as robotaxis close in

key_facts.fact: Uber will lay off about 3,300 employees, or 10% of staff, its largest cuts since the COVID-19 pandemic, announced in a note from CEO Dara Khosrowshahi on Wednesday, September 2.
key_facts.excerpt: Uber Technologies will lay off about 3,300 employees, or 10% of staff, in its largest cuts since the COVID-19 pandemic, to better navigate the rise of robotaxis encroaching on its ride-hailing business.

key_facts.fact: The restructuring cuts the number of employees sitting seven or more reporting layers below the CEO by 20% and reduces 'micro-teams' with only one or two direct reports by nearly half.
key_facts.excerpt: In all, we've reduced the number of employees who sit 7+ [layers below the CEO] by 20% and [cut the] number of micro-teams by nearly 5[0%].

key_facts.fact: Uber is also ending most remote work: it is asking the vast majority of remote employees to move to an office, leaving only about 1% remote, and will concentrate teams in a smaller number of hubs led by New York and San Francisco.
key_facts.excerpt: We are also asking the vast majority of remote employees to move to an office, and going forward, only ~1% of employees will be remote. We'll also continue to reinforce compliance with our hybrid work policy, which requires three days a week in the office.

key_facts.fact: Headcount falls from roughly 34,000 at the end of last year to just under 30,000, roughly where Uber stood in 2021; the last deeper cut was May 2020, when it let go about 6,700 people.
key_facts.excerpt: Uber had roughly 34,000 employees at the end of last year. After this round, headcount drops to just under 30,000, which is about where the company stood in 2021. The last time Uber cut deeper was May 2020, when it let go of about 6,700 people.

key_facts.fact: Khosrowshahi framed the cuts as a response to complexity rather than weak results, writing that Uber's top line has nearly tripled in five years but that growth brought 'more layers, more coordination, more fragmented ownership'; the company is merging its engineering, science and delivery divisions.
key_facts.excerpt: Khosrowshahi's email said the company is combining its engineering, science and delivery divisions. The company is also bringing together its delivery operations across restaurants, retail and direct divisions.

key_facts.fact: Savings from the leaner organisation are meant to be reinvested in growth and innovation, including the autonomous future, according to the memo.
key_facts.excerpt: It will also generate savings that we intend to reinvest in growth, innovation, and the capabilities that will matter most over the coming years.

stories.headline: Fed governor Barr backs a rate hike if inflation doesn't ease, pushing September odds near 70%

key_facts.fact: Speaking at a banking forum in Washington on Tuesday, September 1, Fed Governor Michael Barr said in prepared remarks he would be prepared to support an interest rate hike if inflation does not ease.
key_facts.excerpt: Fed Governor Michael Barr said Tuesday he would back a rate hike unless inflation shows convincing signs it is moving back to the central bank's 2% target.

key_facts.fact: Barr's line: 'If trends in the data give me some confidence that inflation is moderating on a path to 2%, then I think we can take a bit more time to assess our policy stance. However, if inflation appears not to be moderating sufficiently, then I think we should act decisively to raise rates.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'If trends in the data give me some confidence that inflation is moderating on a path to 2%, then I think we can take a bit more time to assess our policy stance,' Barr said in prepared remarks. 'However, if inflation appears not to be moderating sufficiently, then I think we should act decisively to raise rates.'

key_facts.fact: US inflation has been stuck above the Fed's 2% target for nearly five and a half years; the latest readings showed headline prices up 3.7% over the past year and 3.3% excluding food and energy.
key_facts.excerpt: he's concerned about 'broader price pressures taking hold' as inflation has remained stuck above the Fed's 2% target for nearly 5½ years. ... The most recent inflation readings showed headline prices up 3.7% over the past year, or 3.3% excluding food and energy.

key_facts.fact: As of Tuesday's open CME FedWatch put the odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 16 FOMC meeting at roughly 65-68%, up from about 36% before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech on August 28.
key_facts.excerpt: As of the open Tuesday, CME FedWatch places September rate-hike odds at approximately 65–68%, more than doubling from the roughly 36% priced in before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address last Friday.

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.79% on Tuesday, its highest level since January 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year Treasury yield — the anchor for 30-year fixed mortgage pricing, auto loans, and corporate borrowing — rose to approximately 4.79% Tuesday, its highest level since January 2025.

key_facts.fact: The FOMC held the target range at 3.50%-3.75% in late July; a quarter-point September move would lift it to 3.75%-4.00%. Prediction-market pricing for at least one 2026 hike rose to about 72% after Barr's remarks, from 68% after Jackson Hole.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Open Market Committee held the target range at 3.50% to 3.75% at the late-July meeting. ... Prediction-market traders now put the chance of at least one rate increase before the end of 2026 around 72%. That is up from 68% after the late-August Jackson Hole remarks.

key_facts.fact: The August jobs report due September 4 is the last major release before the decision; July payrolls contracted by 23,000, and Bloomberg Economics has noted there is no modern precedent for the Fed hiking after two consecutive negative payroll prints.
key_facts.excerpt: July's payrolls came in at negative 23,000, a surprise contraction. Bloomberg Economics' Anna Wong observed on August 29 that 'there is no modern Fed era precedent of Fed hiking after two negative payrolls prints.'

stories.headline: Brazil's Q2 GDP beats forecasts at 0.5% but household consumption falls for the first time in years

key_facts.fact: Brazil's GDP grew 0.5% in the April-June quarter from the previous quarter, statistics agency IBGE said on Tuesday, September 1 — slower than the 1.1% first-quarter expansion but above the 0.4% median in a Reuters poll of economists.
key_facts.excerpt: Gross domestic product in Latin America's largest economy grew 0.5% in the April-June period from the previous quarter, statistics agency IBGE said on Tuesday. That was slower than the 1.1% expansion in the first quarter but above the 0.4% forecast in a Reuters poll of economists.

key_facts.fact: On an annual basis GDP rose 2.0% in the second quarter, also beating expectations for a 1.8% increase; output totalled R$3.4 trillion in current values.
key_facts.excerpt: On an annual basis, GDP rose 2.0% in the second quarter, also beating expectations for a 1.8% increase.

key_facts.fact: Agriculture carried the quarter, growing 2.8%, while services rose just 0.2% and industry 0.1%; on the demand side investment rose 1.2%, government consumption 0.4%, exports fell 0.8% and imports rose 1.8%.
key_facts.excerpt: O crescimento entre abril e junho foi puxado principalmente pela agropecuária, que avançou 2,8% ... Os serviços cresceram 0,2% e a indústria, 0,1%. Pelo lado da demanda, os investimentos cresceram 1,2% e o consumo do governo aumentou 0,4%. Já o consumo das famílias caiu 0,4%.

key_facts.fact: Household consumption contracted 0.4% in the quarter — its first drop in years — as double-digit interest rates and high household debt weighed on families.
key_facts.excerpt: Warning sign: Household consumption fell 0.4 percent in the quarter, its first drop in years, as double-digit interest rates weigh on families.

key_facts.fact: Brazil's Finance Ministry, which currently forecasts 2.3% growth in 2026, said after the release that it was reviewing that estimate for its next macroeconomic report with a downward bias.
key_facts.excerpt: Brazil's Finance Ministry currently forecasts 2.3% growth in 2026, but said after the release that it was reviewing that estimate for its next macroeconomic report, with a downward bias.

key_facts.fact: Economists said the composition points to near-stagnation ahead: the statistical carryover for 2026 growth stands at 1.8%, and forecasters including C6 Bank (1.7%), MB Associados (1.8%) and BRCG (cut to 1.7%) see the slowdown deepening.
key_facts.excerpt: Economists said the figures reinforce expectations that activity will be close to stagnation over the next two quarters. After the second-quarter release, the statistical carryover for GDP growth in 2026 stood at 1.8%.

key_facts.fact: The data landed the same day the government sent its 2027 budget bill to Congress, one month before the general election.
key_facts.excerpt: Political timing: The data landed on the same day the government sent its 2027 budget to Congress, one month before the general election.
